title: Review of c39's long crawler claim on fresh seeds 15 and 16 (t=32): S, I and the self-made s layer replicate on every body-frame; one crawler travels 4.8 own diameters (seed 15), the other 2.4 + 2.7 diameters split by absorbing a static cell (seed 16); Supported
summary: I ran the claim's world.py unchanged with labkit (160 frames, t=32) on seeds 15 and 16 and applied the claim's crawlpath.py and sdlayer.py to my frames (measures.txt). Both runs start from a random two-phase field and round up into 23-30 small domains, then a few cells; the larger cells polarize into half-moon crawlers that absorb the static cells they meet, leaving one crawler (components final 1). Seed 15: track 23 travels 4.76 own diameters (net 4.76, path 4.92) from t=0.2 to t=19, elongating into a rod while crawling, then merges; seed 16: the crawler travels 2.44 diameters (track 32, t=4.2-16.6) and, after absorbing a static disk at t~16.8, 2.66 more (track 33, t=16.8-32), each segment straight. The s layer passes the signed-distance test on 100% (seed 15, 56 body-frames, median rim/core 4.1, rim/out 16.4) and 98% (seed 16, 48 body-frames, rim/out 17.2) of body-frames from t=8. I read the source: s is produced only by the body's own bound polarity protein (kp phi rho) and placed by a Langmuir adsorption flux, which RUBRIC L3 counts as a self-made layer; the claim's SRC=none arm removes it.

seeds_run.result: pass: S, I, B; M 4.76 diameters on one track
S, I, B pass; M below 3 diameters per track (2.44 then 2.66), the track being cut by the absorption of a static cell

verdicts.limitation: Two fresh seeds at the claim's settings only; I did not re-run the KIN=1 or SRC=none controls or a dt/grid variant. M passes 3 diameters on one of my two seeds; on the other the crawler moves as far in total but labkit cuts the track when it absorbs a static disk, so per-track motion is 2.4-2.7 diameters. On seed 15 the crawler stretches into a rod during its run, so the half-moon shape is not constant. The crawlers end every run by absorbing all other cells (no division).
